en: O, Dark Star.
What!?
Become a dark path that shall\nwhisk him away!!
W-what is this!?
Wh-what's happening!? What's\ngoing on!
Big sister Eve!? What are you\ndoing!?
Tika! Get back! This summoning\nis...!

The Captain and the others
should be able to handle this
opponent. Keep them occupied
for a while.
...And then, leave the <font color=yellow>Azurite\nStar System</font>.
Eve!? What are you talking\nabout!
I don't understand! Why would\nyou do this...!
That summoning...!! That\nsummoning belongs to him...
That wasn't Givel's summon!!
Captain, Verda, Coro...\neveryone.
Goodbye.
Eve!
Captain! We have reached the\ntarget sector.

Yes, it looks like the warp-out
was a success. Is there
anything dangerous in the
vicinity?
There are countless spacecraft\nother than ours in the\nsurrounding sector.

I've confirmed warnings via wide-area
communication. They are demanding
our purpose for passing through the
sector and a declaration that we are a
neutral vessel!
Just as expected. Who is the\ncommunication from?

Analysis complete. The
wide-area communications are
being sent simultaneously by
both factions.
Which one is closer?

Combat units from both factions
capable of reaching this ship are
rapidly approaching from Course 93,
Mark 3, and Mark 182!
Identification signals have been\nverified!

I've confirmed the <font color=yellow>Planet Raza</font>
Space Force approaching from
Mark 182, and the <font color=yellow>Planet Ober</font>
Space Force fleet from Mark 3!
I see. I didn't expect both Raza\nand Ober to show up at the\nsame time...
I wonder if either of them\nmight be friendly?

Nope, I'm picking up fire-control
locks. Both sides are gonna
open fire in less than 100
seconds!

They are even more aggressive
than the rumors suggested.
They're hardly giving us a
chance to speak.
All crew harnesses are locked.\nWe are prepared for any\nsudden combat maneuvers.
Now, we simply have to do\neverything in our power.
You're right. Captain, are you\nready?
Very well, I will send a\nwide-range transmission back.\nOver to you, <font color=yellow>Heath</font>...
Roger! Leave the rest to me.

This is Ensign Heath of the
Heath Bureau, assigned to the
Planet Raza Space Force
combat ship Isabel,
I am currently on a mission to\nescort war refugees from\nPlanet Ober.
Our destination is the neutral\nasteroid belt, <font color=yellow>Stardust Bazaar</font>.

Pursuant to Article 100 of the Wartime
Agreement, we request an immediate
cessation of hostilities. I repeat, this is
the Planet Raza Space Force...
Sorry, but enough with the\nspeech!!
Optical weapons launch\nconfirmed from Mark 182!
Switching to evasive\nmaneuvers! All crew, brace for\nimpact!
High-speed projectiles\nconfirmed from Mark 3 as well!
No response from either fleet!\nLooks like we're being ignored!
It can't be helped! We're\nbreaking through! Everyone,\nhold on tight!

To have this little shake during
such a maneuver... what an
incredible inertia cancel
function...

You can praise me more than
that! All enemy optical weapon
fire has been successfully
evaded!
You idiot, where the hell are\nyou looking?!
What?! Did something graze\nus?!

I've confirmed something
attached to the fleet's outer
hull. It looks like a projectile
fired by the Ober army!
Something attached...? Bringing\nup the screen!
Eek! What is that? It's\ndisgusting!
Those are the Ober army's\n<font color=yellow>Wormhole Insects</font>!

What! Hostile biological signatures
inside the ship?! And there's even an
oxygen leak warning... but the outer hull
isn't damaged anywhere!
Wormhole Insects are biological\nweapons used for raiding ships.

They can move through subspace,
allowing them to infiltrate a ship
without damaging the shields or the
outer hull!
You mean the oxygen is leaking\nthrough subspace?! What is\nthis creepy feeling!

Eve: This is no time for whining!
They're already inside, so let's
just get to work and
exterminate these pests!
Rekoro: "No time for whining"?!\nEve, these are bugs! BUGS!!
We must ensure the safety of\nthe crew! Where have they\ninfiltrated?!
Looks like a fair number of 'em\nare near the passengers!
Rekoro: They've spread out all\nover the place too! This is just\nso gross!!
Tika! Transfer the location\ndata of the intruders.
Rekoro! Got it! What's the\nplan?!
Ewin Laxter and Welch\nVineyard will handle the\ndefense of the passengers!
Mastima and Karlyn Kayson\nwill eliminate the remaining\nintruders!!
Transfer the ship's data! I will\nnavigate for Mastima and the\nothers!
These are the points where the\nforeign entities entered. Can\nyou eliminate them?
I wonder who you're asking.\nThis few won't even be a\nproper warm-up.

Space-eating insects... how
fascinating. I'll capture a few
alive; they'll make excellent
research material.

Your confidence is reassuring! Now,
Mastima, Karlyn Kayson, and I shall
head to the various sections of the
ship to eliminate the intruders!
I leave the defense of the\nhangar in your hands!
Roger that! Leave it to me!
Space bugs are a piece of\ncake! Bring it on!
Beasts! Protect our ship!\nSparkling Stars!!
Oops, looks like they've already\nshown up over here!
Eww, gross! Let's just get rid\nof them quickly!
Alright, that should do it!
Finished already? How\nanticlimactic! Bring on more!!
Don't be ridiculous. I can't\nspend all day dealing with\nthings like this.
Huh? Are you already done\nover there?
I can confirm that all reactions\nwithin the ship have been\neliminated...
Master Mastima: These are\ncreatures that sneak into ships\nunnoticed.

Master Mastima: If even one is
overlooked, there is no telling
what kind of trouble it could
cause. Stay vigilant.
At least the "passengers" seem\nto be safe. Hey, what's the\nstatus of the ship?

Based on data cross-referenced with
the AI Rekoro, it appears Lady Carlin
and Master Mastima have cleared the
intruders from their respective sectors.
Perfect timing. The enemy\nforces ahead have begun\nfighting among themselves.
I believe we should take\nadvantage of this chaos to exit\nthe combat zone.

Agreed. Let's get moving then.
Rekoro, can you guide Karlyn
and the others to the
harnesses?
Understood.
Roger that! Full speed ahead\nto exit the combat zone!
Destination: Stardust Bazaar\nin the Azurite system. Here we\ngo!!
...Damn, those guys are no\njoke...!
...It looks like we managed to\nshake them off.
No anomalies in the surrounding space.\nNo obstacles detected between here\nand our destination. We are safe now.
I am glad everyone is safe...\nbut I cannot believe they\nactually fired at both of us...

We identified our affiliations
and goals, and we used an
open communication channel,
right?

Even so, I can't believe they
would attack the Raza Space
Force, which Heath is
supposed to be a part of.
My apologies. To be honest, I\nnever imagined they would\nattack with such hesitation...
Well, that's just how it goes\nwhen a third-party ship shows\nup in a combat zone.
Brother...

Heath said it himself. If what he and his
people are doing comes to light, it'll be
a massive scandal for the Raza Space
Force.
When someone like that just\nwanders in defenseless, anyone\nwould want to silence them.
But that's different from\nactually doing it, isn't it?

Stop being so naive. If you honestly tell
them you're carrying war refugees from
Planet Ober, it'd be weirder if they
didn't attack.
To the soldiers of Planet Raza,\nOberians are prisoners of war,\nnot refugees to be protected.
Big brother! You're going too\nfar!
...No, Ricardo is right. I was\nnaive. This is the reality of this\nstar system.

That's not true! The ones who
are wrong are the Raza and
Ober armies for not listening to
Mr. Heath!
Mr. Heath isn't wrong for trying\nto help war refugees who were\nsuffering right in front of him!
The people who stay on the\nright path always win! They\nhave to win!
The world is a miserable place\nprecisely because that's not\nalways the case.
You've seen that enough\nyourself back in Daftine.
...That's true.

But because I want the world to be as
Tika describes, I agreed with Ricardo to
cooperate with him back then. Isn't that
right?
...Tch.
Ensign Heath. I hope you won't\ntake this the wrong way.
While there are various opinions, we are\nall in agreement that this ship will\nsupport your mission to the end.
No, I haven't doubted that for\na single second.
It's just that... sometimes I can\nonly think about things in a\nvery straightforward way.

That's why I believe the opinions of
someone like Ricardo, who can stay
calm even if they're a bit cynical, are
so important!
It's a relief to hear you say\nthat.
...Hey. Who are you calling\ncynical...?
Ah, no, I didn't mean it in a bad\nway... I just...
Captain! Stardust Bazaar will\nbe within visual range on the\nscreen shortly.

I've also picked up an
identification signal that
appears to be coming from the
Bazaar.

Understood. Checking
communications. I have
confirmed that the Stardust
Bazaar has no hostile intent.

The Stardust Bazaar... the only
completely neutral zone
remaining in the Azurite system
during this time of war.
I suppose we can finally take a\nbreather now, eh?
Yes. I guess so.
...If we couldn't, we'd be\nseriously screwed...

The ship has entered a safe
zone. It appears we will arrive
at our destination, the
Stardust Bazaar, shortly.
I see. Finally, a moment of\npeace. I'm just glad everyone is\nsafe.

Not "safe" at all! What was that
about?! Heath told them
everything, but they both
attacked us anyway!
And they did it knowing that...\nthat there are refugees from\nOber here!!
Ugh, it makes me so mad!
Eu! We're stopping it! This\ninterstellar war between Raza\nand Ober!
What?! Just like that?!
What?! Don't tell me you're\ngetting cold feet just because\nthe scale is galactic!

No, it's just... we don't even know what
kind of war it is yet. Making a
declaration like that in front of the
people from Ober is a bit...
What happened to the Eu who\nrisked everything to stop the\nHoly War!
A holy war and an interstellar\nwar are basically the same\nthing!

Anyone who shoots people just trying
to live their lives under the sun might
be forgiven by the heavens, but they'll
never be forgiven by me!
Alright, alright, I get it! Just\ncalm down before the ship jolts\nand you bite your tongue!

Fine! You lot better keep your heads
held high too! No matter how hard
things get, as long as you've got the
spirit of a weed, a path will open―glub!
Aaaaagh!!! I bit my tongue!!!
Lycanthrope Boy: ...Spirit... of a\nweed.
...Do whatever you want...\n*Sigh*.

Escorting war refugees from
the planet Ober... Heath said
our help was only needed up to
this point, but...
Stardust Bazaar, Terminal Port\ncontrol has granted landing\npermission.
GFSS-3214F, landing at\nStardust Bazaar.
Hehe... finally... When those\nWormhole Insects showed up, I\nseriously thought it was over...
Hehe, good work, Heath.
Oh, right. Thank you!

Now I can give the boss... er, my
superior, a basic mission report!
Captain, I thank you from the bottom of
my heart on behalf of my superior!
Ensign Heath Bureau of the\nRaza Space Force...
I wonder why he possesses the\nsame human DNA as the\nCaptain...
I hope there is some useful\ninformation to be found here in\nthe Stardust Bazaar.
14 days ago
Coro. Coro! Where are you?
Captain, do you know where\nCoro is?
Huh? In a place like this... Now\nwe're talking! Coro! Coro! Coro!!
...Click.
Awa wa wa wa wa wa wa!!

Man, this is handy. Mastima's
greatest achievement has to
be creating this Coro Rampage
Suppression Device!
Hey, this is a violation of AI\nrights!

I wasn't even rampaging; I was
just taking a peaceful nap...
Everyone always pushes the
button just for fun...
I think the problem lies with\nCoro for doing things that\nmake people want to push it.
More importantly, Captain,\nCoro―do you know where\nRicardo is?
More importantly... how cruel!

Aye. Valka, over in the analysis room,
told me that some space-faring vessels
are engaged in combat in the sector
ahead.
Combat? My standard sensors\nhaven't detected anything yet.
She said it's only a faint signal\non the ultra-long-range\nsensors.

So, while she was waking Coro up, she
mentioned she wanted Ricardo, as a
former fire control officer, to help
analyze the situation.
In that case, I'll allocate my\nfunctions to the analysis room\nwhere Valka is.
It looks like Ricardo is still\nresting in his room, so I'll send\nhim a message.
I'm counting on you.
...Still, Coro.
Yes? What is it?
If this had been the Coro from\na while back, the moment you\nheard "combat,"

you would've been shouting
about fleeing or evading
immediately... You've really
grown, haven't you...!

Hehe! Now, both I and this GFSS-3214F
possess ultra-high-spec functions that
are second to none, even compared to
the Galactic Federation's latest combat
ships!

As long as I'm around, we'll be unstoppable in
this universe! No matter what emergency arises,
I'll use my processing power to instantly derive
the optimal solution to resolve the situation!
So please, Captain, just sit\nback in your chair and relax\nwhile you enjoy a banana...
*Click.*
Awa-wa-wa-wa-wa!!
With all that processing power\nyou brag about, how did you\nfail to predict this result...?
Come on, just this once...
Well, jokes aside, it would be\nbest to gather everyone on the\nBridge.
Indeed. The journey to return\nTika and the others to their\nhome has only just begun.
Now that our party has grown,\nwe must proceed with caution.
Alright, here's a report on the\nanalysis results. Not exactly\nexciting news.

Based on our findings, it is presumed
that an interstellar war between
advanced planets is currently taking
place in the Azurite system, our target
destination.
Interstellar war? You mean\nentire planets are at war? Is\nthat even possible!?

If you think of a single planet
as an island or a country, I
suppose that kind of thing
could happen.

However, when it comes to a war on a
cosmic scale, the distribution and
density of the battlefield differ
significantly from wars fought on a
planet's surface.

With a ship like this, I believe we won't
encounter much danger as long as we
avoid the sectors where combat is
occurring.
Exactly. We're heading for the\nStardust Bazaar in the Azurite\nsystem.
The area around it seemed\npeaceful. The combat zones\nare likely strictly designated.
But to reach the Stardust\nBazaar,

we've found that no matter
which route we take, we'll have
to cross a combat zone for at
least 90 minutes.
We'll need to keep our guard at\nmaximum during that time.
Captain, Administrator Koro.

Captain, Administrator Coro, please
notify all crew members to be seated in
their harnessed seats before we enter
the sector.
You got it! I'll let the members\nwho aren't on the Bridge know\nright away!
...Wait, why is half the crew\nmissing? I told you this was an\nimportant announcement.
I saw Eve and Karlyn heading\ninto the medical bay together a\nlittle while ago.

Now that you mention it, I
heard Tika and Rekoro saying
they were going to the medical
bay too.
I saw Verda being dragged into\nthe medical bay by Mastima\nearlier.
Just shove them all into\nmedical pods if it comes down\nto it.
Tika too?
Are you serious? Or are you\nbeing sarcastic?
I think they're doing that thing\nthey've been doing ever since\nwe left Daftine.

Apparently, their research
hasn't been going well lately, so
Eve, Karlyn, and Mastima have
been fighting a lot.

So Tika and Verda are acting
as lookouts to step in and
mediate if things get out of
hand.
Good grief... I can't tell which of\nthem are the kids.
It's perfectly normal for\nresearch not to go smoothly.
That's exactly when the real\nchallenge is staying calm and\ncomposed!!
And how do you handle things\nin those moments, Welch?
You're asking that knowing full\nwell the answer, aren't you?

Anyway, I've delivered the
important news. I'll leave it to
you all to deal with the ones
who weren't listening.
It can't be helped. Captain,\nshall we head to the infirmary?
Given the situation, I'd like one\nof the ladies to accompany\nus...

On second thought, never mind. I have
a feeling that if something is happening
in the infirmary, it'll only make things
more complicated.
Valka & Welch: Did you say\nsomething!?
Did you say something!?
Eek!? No, nothing! I'll be going\nnow!!
Now then, I just hope nothing's\nhappened...
And there it is, right as I said\nit...
Another one of those gurgling\nthings came out! Sister Verda,\nover there!
How many times is this now?!\nThis is why I said we should\nuse the Battle Simulator!

Hearing gunfire coming from
the infirmary... this is basically
a riot, isn't it? What do you
want to do, Captain?
Pretend I didn't see and turn\nback
I can't just ignore this
Are you sure? Something\ndefinitely bad is happening.
True. They aren't the type of\npeople who'll calm down just\nbecause you tell them to.
In that case, shall we contact\nthem individually once the\nstorm has passed?

Hmph! Captain! Coro! What are
you doing?! Don't you dare
leave us in this state, you
heartless people!!
W-what on earth is all this\ncommotion about?!
Ah! Captain! Coro! Sorry! This\nis the last one in Gerel!
That's not the point!

Mastima! You did another one
of your incomprehensible
experiments and failed, didn't
you?!
Hmm? I didn't fail. I felt like I\nwas just a little bit away from\nsuccess.
Mastima!!
All right! That's the end of\nthem!
*Huff*... *puff*... Somehow, we\nmanaged to exterminate them...
Oh boy, how am I going to\nexplain this disaster to Karlyn\nand Eve when they wake up?
...What on earth were you all\ndoing?
Tika and Verda are showing\nsigns of extreme fatigue.
To ensure an accurate report, I\nshall explain the situation.
Please... though honestly, I\ndon't really want to hear it.

<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> Captain, Coro, I believe you are
both aware that Mastima has been
conducting extensive research into the
summoning crests of Evelysse and
Karlyn Kayson.

<font color=blue>Mastima</font> And this latest
incident is a splendid result
obtained during the course of
that research!
<font color=blue>Coro</font> You're calling this\ndisaster a "result"?!

<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> The main points of the
experiment were twofold: first, to
determine how the coordinates of the
summoning source and destination are
established,

and second, to observe what
changes occur within the crest
during the coordinate fixation
process.

To that end, we established a new
experimental biological containment
zone on the ship, where we kept Gerel
for summoning experiments.
<font color=blue>Coro</font> Why on earth is there a\nfacility like that that neither\nthe Captain nor I knew about?!
<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> Mastima claimed that\npermission had been granted.

<font color=blue>Coro</font> You know as well as I do,
Rekoro, that she's not the type
of person to actually do
something so proper!
<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> Regardless, the\nexperiment involved using the\ncaptive Gerel

to see if it was possible to
summon them from
containment capsule A to
containment capsule B.
<font color=blue>Coro</font> ...And then, you failed to\nspecify the coordinates, and\nthe Gerel leaked out. That's it.
<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> Affirmative!
<font color=blue>Coro</font> Then why are Eve and\nKarlyn still asleep in the middle\nof all this chaos?

<font color=blue>Tika</font> Well, Mastima hasn't been able to
fully copy the two of their Gems yet. It
seems like she can't even see half of
the actual form.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> So, she decided that we\nfirst needed to observe the\nphenomenon in detail...
...and she suggested conducting the\nexperiment by disconnecting the Gems\nfrom Eve and Karlyn's consciousness.
For the record, I was against it.\nI only found out about the\nGerel capsules today.

<font color=blue>Coro</font> Please don't do such terrifying
experiments in outer space... At least
do it on the surface of a planet with an
atmosphere...
Huh?
Mm... *yawn*... Is it over?
It looks like it... mmm...
Wha?! W-what happened?! The\ninfirmary is a complete mess!

...Judging by the look on Verda
and the others' faces, it's
obvious that things didn't go
well.
I assume the Captain and Coro\nonly came because they\nsmelled trouble.
Yes, well, that's about right.
For the record, this was\nabsolutely not a failure!
Wah!
We simply discovered that this\nparticular method would not\nwork.

Today, the research into these
two's summoning crests took
another step forward. You
should be celebrating.
How am I supposed to\ncelebrate while looking at this\ndisaster...?
Typical scientist's sophistry...

It's only been two months since
we left Daftine. I didn't expect
the secrets of these crests to
be revealed so easily.
So, whether it was a success\nor a failure doesn't really\nmatter to me.
It was a success!
Yes, yes. I'm the one who\nasked for the analysis, after all.

But I don't want to put my
comrades in danger just to find
out the true nature of my
power.

If I'm causing too much trouble
for the Captain and the others,
I'm perfectly fine with you
shutting down my research.
What!!
Well, I'll be going now. Call me\nagain when you think of the\nnext experiment.
M-Mastima? Um...
Tikaaa! She was being\nsarcastic! That was totally\nsarcastic!
And I'm working so hard! I'm\nworking so haaaaard!
...I think that's exactly the\nproblem.
I'm sorry things turned out so\nweird.
Hm? A message for us? Did\nsomething happen?
An interstellar war in the\nAzurite system... huh.
It means everyone needs to\nget to a safe spot before we\nenter the combat zone.
By the way, why are we even\ngoing there?

In Tika's era, the Azurite system
contains an independent autonomous
asteroid belt known as the Stardust
Bazaar.
The Azurite system achieved\nspace development earlier than\nthe Daft system.

Consequently, the Stardust
Bazaar has long been a hub for
various information from the
surrounding star systems.

We talked about going there first
because there might be a hint on how
to return Tika and Ricardo to their own
time, remember?
Didn't we already discuss this?
Right. Humans weren't around\nthere 10,000 years ago,

and I figured if it was only 200
years in the future, they could
just use cold sleep. I might not
have been listening closely.
It is not as simple as Tika and\nRicardo just traveling 200\nyears into the future.

Both of them have spent a
great deal of time in the past
timeline and have grown since
then.
We must be very careful about\nthe point in time we send them\nback to.

Also, if we send them back before they
board the transport ship Kugo and they
make contact with the Tika and Ricardo
of that era,
there is a possibility that Tika\nand Ricardo might decide not\nto board the transport ship.
To absolutely prevent a time\nparadox,
we should return them only\nafter Tika and Ricardo have\ndeparted from Daftine.

However, even then, I have
heard that Daftine was under
attack by some force at that
time.
I do not know the state of the\nsatellite Mastima during that\nperiod,

but it would be a disaster if
they were to enter cold sleep
in a location that was about to
be attacked.
There is no point in sending\nthem back if the location is not\nabsolutely safe...

Yeah, yeah, I get it. Anyway, for
various reasons, you're heading
to the Azurite system. That's
all I need to know.
Now, Evelysse. Let us continue\nthe experiment. Everyone else,\nplease leave.
Ah, wait!
Unyah!!
Nuuh!
Hey, Mastima! I'm talking about\nthat part!
But why... Why can't I grasp\nany of this...?

I am the one most versed in
Gems in all of Paradise...! To
think I cannot decode such a
simple Gem for months...!
Mastima, are you listening?\nYou don't have to be so\ndepressed.
Depressed!? I am furious! At\nmy own incompetence!

It is by no means complex! The
grammar consists of things
that have existed since the era
of Planet Nede!
Look here! This part right here\nis a Gem that is the absolute\nbasics of basics!
I'm sorry. Even if you tell me, I\ndon't understand...

Ggg... Fine, I admit it. At first, I
underestimated it. There are
plenty of Gems that can
teleport matter.
I naively assumed that brat,\nGiverese, had simply stolen my\nknowledge to complete it!
And yet, what on earth is with\nyour Gems!

The crest on Karlyn Kayson's
skin, and the one etched into
your genetic information, are
both incredibly simple!

And yet, they overlap in a way that
should be absolutely impossible! It's like
a key fitting a lock it shouldn't! Like oil
and water mixing!
Curse you all!
Now, Mastima, let's take a little\nbreak.

We're staying in the Bazaar for a while,
so you can just set aside more time for
tests and research later, right? We
have other things to do right now.
Ugh... If only, if only I had one\nmore sample...
It has to be here. The key to\nsolving this mystery...
I'm sure I've seen something\nvery similar to this structure\nsomewhere before...
Just one more... just one\nmore...
Hello? Mastima, are you\nlistening?
...Giverese.
Huh?
Evelysse. Where did you send\nGiverese back then?
What do you mean, "where did I\nsend..."?

During the battle in the gap
between worlds, you made
Giverese vanish into the light
without using "Summon."
Was that an unconscious\naction?

That creature was also a being
capable of summoning. Though
in a different form than you or
Karlyn Kayson.
It may be the final key. Answer\nme, Evelysse.
Back then... you didn't kill it, did\nyou?
That's...!
What was that thing you\nshowed us?
Was it a Summon? Or... an\nExpulsion?
Geez... Captain, Coro, Verda, I'm\nsorry.
There is no need for Tika to\napologize.
That's right. But please, I'm\nbegging you, stop keeping\nGerel in storage...

They say people become childlike as
they age, but I suppose that's what
happens when you're 3.7 billion years
old. Honestly...
Hm?

signal has been received from
the outer edge of the Azurite
system!	machine
